status: 1-VS-3 LANE OPEN: push_of_war is the project's first non-free-for-all minigame, and I tuned + verified it myself after its builder died (provider retirement). Fixed four real defects my own probes caught: (1) matches ended in 0.6s — the velocity integrator ran ~500x the pace an 8s race needs; (2) the tie-out path handed the solo a free win; (3) the human's taps were weaker than an idle CPU teammate (8 taps/s = 0.13 push/step vs 0.185) so mashing barely mattered — taps now carry their own value on both sides; (4) the stage was invisible — a 20-unit field with characters at x=+/-6 inside a portrait viewport that only shows ~8 units, so vision saw an empty court with a crate. Refit the field, widened the FOV, and eased the crate travel so a narrow lead reads as movement. Verified: solo 38-42% / trio 42-44% / 12-19% tie-outs over 12-24 seeds, twins byte-identical, mashing flips outcomes, payout exactly one winner +10, tsc 0, zero console errors. Audio completion agent still running (level parity, dead-track wiring, ducking).

pieces.name: projectToScreen fix (floats + all ceremony effects land on screen)
pieces.detail: FIXED + COMMITTED. Proven root cause: camera.matrixWorldInverse is stale when projectToScreen runs during update() (three.js updates it inside renderer.render()). Raw proof: char world (-10.6, 0, -7.1) -> ndc x -1.897 -> screen x -175 (matches the critic's ~-193). Fix: cam.updateMatrixWorld() + matrixWorldInverse.copy(matrixWorld).invert() before projecting, plus a null guard for off-screen/behind-camera points. Verified: floats -190 -> +69 (in viewport), sparkles 45/45 on screen, confetti 52/80, banner confirmed, vision: 'entire screen is covered in falling confetti ... denser than a classic Mario Party star buy'. Guards: probe-title ok, twin MATCH, tsc 0, build ok, zero errors.
